findings: Revenue is highly concentrated: the top 20% of customers generate 74.6% of all revenue (£6.52M).
KMeans isolates a VIP cluster of 686 customers (avg 13.94 orders, £8,169 each) that alone drives 64.14% of revenue.
65.3% of customers are repeat buyers — a strong, retention-friendly base to build loyalty programs on.
The UK accounts for 82.9% of revenue; international markets (Netherlands, EIRE, Germany, France) are small but proven — a growth lever.
£510,265 of annual revenue sits in the 'At Risk (high value)' segment — 195 formerly strong customers who have gone quiet.

recommendations.action: Protect & reward: early access, VIP tier, personal account care.
recommendations.why: 984 customers ≈ 67.85% of revenue. Churn here is the single biggest financial risk.

recommendations.action: Win-back campaign: targeted re-engagement offer + 'we miss you' outreach.
recommendations.why: £510,265 of revenue at stake. Recovering just 20% is ≈ £102,053/yr for the cost of one email campaign.

recommendations.action: Nurture up: cross-sell bundles and a points program to push toward Champion status.
recommendations.why: Largest mid-tier group — the pipeline that replenishes the VIP base.

recommendations.action: Low-cost reactivation only (automated flows); don't over-invest.
recommendations.why: 946 customers but only 2.78% of revenue — cap spend and let most lapse.

notes: Dec 2011 is a partial month (data ends 2011-12-09); its month-over-month drop is a data artifact, not a real decline.
